name: PS2 Web Recomp
cost: Free and open source (MIT). You need your own copy of the game
works_with: Chrome or Edge with WebGPU. Builds have been run on Linux on x86-64
short: Turns a PS2 disc you own into a web page that plays the game in your browser, with the game's CPU code recompiled to WebAssembly.
what: PS2 Web Recomp translates a PlayStation 2 game's main CPU code into C++ ahead of time and compiles it to WebAssembly. The rest of the console is emulated, and graphics are drawn with WebGPU. Gran Turismo 4 and God of War II play from boot through races and combat, with sound and a memory card saved in the browser.
who: People comfortable with a C++ toolchain who own PS2 discs and want to see this recompilation approach working. Skip it if you want a general emulator: only two games have been brought up so far, and another game will most likely stop at something not implemented yet.
needs: git, CMake, Ninja, a C++20 compiler (clang is preferred) and Python 3
7-Zip, if your disc image is in a `.7z`
A disc image of a PS2 game you own
About 300 MB of disk space per game
A browser with WebGPU. On Linux, Chrome needs two flags turned on (see the steps)
SDL2 development files, only for the native window build

steps.title: Clone and port a game
steps.text: `port.sh` reads the disc, translates the game's code, runs it headless a few times to find code it missed, then builds the page. The first run installs the Emscripten SDK into `tools/emsdk`.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/snuri00/ps2-web-recomp.git
cd ps2-web-recomp
scripts/port.sh mygame "My Game.iso"
python3 scripts/serve.py build/web-mygame games/mygame/disc.iso    # http://localhost:8620/

steps.title: Open it in your browser
steps.text: Go to `http://localhost:8620/`. On Linux, turn on `chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu` and `chrome://flags/#enable-vulkan` in Chrome and restart it. Without WebGPU the software renderer takes over, which is fine for menus and too slow for 3D.

steps.title: Check how far a new game got
steps.text: Frames from the last exploring run land in `games/mygame/shots`. Use `--press 900:cross` to give your own inputs and `--frames` to set how long each run lasts.

steps.title: Or play it in a native window
steps.text: Build only the native runner with `--native-only`, then start it with your disc. `PS2_SCALE=2` or `3` raises the internal resolution.

try.label: From the README
try.where: The game page, in your browser
try.text: Play with the keyboard: Z, X, A and S are cross, circle, square and triangle, Enter is start and the arrow keys are the D-pad. Then use Export card to download your save as a `.ps2` file you can also load in PCSX2.

watch: No game data is included. Use disc images of games you own.
The generated C++ and WebAssembly are translations of the game, so they belong to the game's owners. The README says to keep them on your own machine and not publish them.
Anyone who can reach the server can load the game, so keep it to yourself.
Only Gran Turismo 4 and God of War II have been brought up. Other games will likely hit an unhandled system call or a missing I/O library and stop.
Saves live in the browser's storage for the address you play from. Export the card if you want a copy.
